name: Angel Reese
description: Angel Reese, born 6 May 2002 in Randallstown, Maryland, is an American professional basketball player for the Atlanta Dream of the WNBA. A McDonald's All-American at Saint Frances Academy in Baltimore, she began her college career at Maryland before transferring to Louisiana State University, where in 2023 she led the Tigers to their first national championship, was the tournament's Most Outstanding Player and set the NCAA single-season record with 34 double-doubles. Chicago drafted her seventh overall in 2024, and her rookie season set league rebounding standards: a record 15 consecutive double-doubles and a league-best 13.1 rebounds per game, followed by a second rebounding title at 12.6 per game in 2025 and a second All-Star selection. Chicago traded her to Atlanta in April 2026. That September she became the first WNBA player to reach 500 rebounds in a single season, and in October 2026 she reached her first WNBA Finals, with Atlanta facing the Golden State Valkyries.

Raised between Cotonou and Lagos, she came to the attention of Mavin Records founder Don Jazzy through the covers and original songs she posted online, signed with Mavin, and released her self-titled debut EP in early 2021. name: Asake
description: Asake, born Ahmed Ololade on 13 January 1995 in Lagos, Nigeria, is a Nigerian singer, rapper and songwriter whose stage name is his mother's name. He studied theatre and dramatic arts at Obafemi Awolowo University and built his sound from Afrobeats, fuji, amapiano and Yoruba street-pop. Olamide signed him to YBNL Nation in February 2022; his debut EP Ololade and the breakthrough single "Omo Ope" followed the same month. His debut album, Mr. Money with the Vibe (2022), set the record for the biggest opening day for an African album on Apple Music at the time and debuted at No. 66 on the Billboard 200, a peak his second album, Work of Art (2023), matched. His third album, Lungu Boy (2024), became his third consecutive No. 1 album in Nigeria and the longest-running No. 1 in Nigerian chart history. He earned Grammy nominations for Best African Music Performance in 2024, for "Amapiano" with Olamide, and in 2025, for "MMS," his collaboration with Wizkid. In February 2025 he left YBNL and launched his own label, Giran Republic; his fourth album, M$NEY, was released on 1 May 2026.

name: Anita Baker
description: Anita Baker, born January 26, 1958, in Toledo, Ohio, and raised in Detroit, Michigan, is an American singer whose three-octave range and emotional delivery made her one of the defining voices of urban contemporary soul and rhythm and blues. She first sang in Detroit church choirs, left community college to perform in nightclubs, and joined the funk group Chapter 8, touring with the band and recording an album that included the single I Just Want to Be Your Girl. After the group was dropped by its label, she stopped performing, then returned for Beverly Glen Records with the solo album The Songstress (1983), which sold more than 300,000 copies. Moving to Elektra, she executive-produced Rapture (1986), which won two Grammy Awards, sold more than five million copies, and produced the hit singles Sweet Love and You Bring Me Joy. Giving You the Best That I Got followed in 1988 and Compositions in 1990; both albums won Grammys. After a hiatus she returned with Rhythm of Love (1994), signed with Atlantic Records in 1996, and released My Everything on Blue Note in 2004. The Recording Academy's artist record credits her with eight Grammy wins from eighteen nominations. She embarked on a farewell tour in 2018.

name: Al Green
aliases: Albert Leornes Greene; The Reverend Al Green
description: Al Green (born Albert Leornes Greene, April 13, 1946, in Forrest City, Arkansas) is an American singer, songwriter, and pastor whose work with producer Willie Mitchell at Memphis’s Hi Records defined early-1970s soul. Raised in a gospel-singing family, later of Grand Rapids, Michigan, Green signed with Hi in 1969; Mitchell coached him away from imitation toward the soft, falsetto-touched voice that became his signature. A run of albums — Al Green Gets Next to You (1971), Let’s Stay Together (1972), I’m Still in Love with You (1972), and Call Me (1973) — produced “Tired of Being Alone,” “Let’s Stay Together,” “I’m Still in Love with You,” and “Love and Happiness,” recorded with the Hi Rhythm Section at Royal Studios. Ordained as a pastor, he turned to gospel in the 1980s, later returning to secular recording. The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, which inducted him in 1995, calls him “one of the most gifted purveyors of soul music.” He has won 11 Grammy Awards, including the Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award.

name: Aaliyah
description: Aaliyah (born Aaliyah Dana Haughton on January 16, 1979, in Brooklyn, New York, and raised in Detroit, Michigan; died August 25, 2001) was an American singer and actress whose cool, understated delivery reshaped contemporary R&B. She released her debut album, Age Ain't Nothing but a Number, in 1994 at age fifteen, then remade her sound with producers Timbaland and Missy Elliott on One in a Million (1996), a record whose futuristic rhythms pointed R&B toward the next decade. She starred opposite Jet Li in Romeo Must Die (2000), and her single from its soundtrack became the first song to top the Billboard Hot 100 based solely on radio airplay. Her third album, Aaliyah (2001), reached No. 1 on the Billboard 200. She died at twenty-two in a plane crash in the Bahamas after filming a music video, leaving a brief catalog whose influence has only grown.

description: André De Shields (born André Robin De Shields, January 12, 1946, in Baltimore, Maryland) is an actor, singer, dancer, director and choreographer whose career on the American stage spans more than five decades. Raised in Baltimore, the ninth of eleven children, he earned a BA in English literature from the University of Wisconsin–Madison (1970) and an MA in African-American studies from New York University's Gallatin School (1991). He originated roles in the Broadway productions of The Wiz (the title role), Ain't Misbehavin', Play On! and The Full Monty — the latter two earning Tony Award nominations — and won a Primetime Emmy Award for the 1982 NBC broadcast of Ain't Misbehavin'. As Hermes in Hadestown he won the 2019 Tony Award for Best Featured Actor in a Musical and the 2020 Grammy Award for Best Musical Theater Album. On October 12, 2026, the African American Film Critics Association presented him its Legacy Award. CultureTechLens profiled the honor in Short #147, published October 14, 2026.

name: Audra McDonald
description: Audra McDonald, born Audra Ann McDonald on 3 July 1970 in West Berlin, Germany, to American parents, and raised in Fresno, California, is an American actress and soprano who has won six Tony Awards, more performance wins than any other actor, and is the only performer to have won in all four Tony acting categories. A Juilliard-trained classical singer (class of 1993), she won her first Tony a year later as Carrie Pipperidge in Carousel, then added Master Class (1996), Ragtime (1998), A Raisin in the Sun (2004), Porgy and Bess (2012) and Lady Day at Emerson's Bar & Grill (2014), in which she embodied Billie Holiday. Her honors extend to a record eleven Tony nominations, two Grammy Awards and a Primetime Emmy Award for hosting Live from Lincoln Center. Television audiences know her as Dr. Naomi Bennett in Private Practice (2007–2011) and as Liz Lawrence in The Good Fight, and her film work includes Beauty and the Beast (2017) and Respect (2021). She received the National Medal of Arts in 2016 and was inducted into the American Theater Hall of Fame in 2017; her 2025 performance as Rose in Gypsy brought her record eleventh Tony nomination.

name: Ava DuVernay
description: Ava DuVernay, born Ava Marie DuVernay on August 24, 1972, in Long Beach, California, is an American filmmaker raised in Lynwood and Compton. She graduated from Saint Joseph High School in Lakewood in 1990 and earned bachelor's degrees in English and African American studies from UCLA in 1995. After an internship with CBS News and a career in film publicity — including her own firm, The DuVernay Agency — she turned to directing. Her second feature, Middle of Nowhere (2012), won the Directing Award at the Sundance Film Festival, making her the first Black woman to receive it. Selma (2014) made her the first Black woman nominated for a Golden Globe for Best Director and the first to direct a film nominated for the Academy Award for Best Picture. Her documentary 13th (2016) was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Documentary Feature, and A Wrinkle in Time (2018) made her the first Black woman to direct a live-action film with a budget of $100 million. She founded the distribution collective ARRAY and created the series Queen Sugar (2016) and When They See Us (2019); Origin (2023) adapted Isabel Wilkerson's Caste.

name: A Different World
description: A Different World, created by Bill Cosby as a spin-off of The Cosby Show and reshaped creatively by Debbie Allen from its second season, aired on NBC from September 24, 1987, to July 9, 1993 — six seasons, 144 episodes set at Hillman College, a fictional historically Black university. A top-five ratings series for four of its six seasons, it used the campus as a license to treat subjects network sitcoms avoided: an HIV/AIDS episode in 1990, and storylines on date rape and colorism, carried by an ensemble that made the HBCU experience visible to a mass audience for the first time. Its cultural footprint is measurable with care: National Center for Education Statistics figures show total HBCU enrollment rising roughly 24 percent during the run (from about 228,000 in 1987 to about 283,000 in 1993), and alumni and cast credit the series with driving college interest — though the data do not establish that the show alone caused the rise, and this record does not claim otherwise. Hillman was fictional; the applications were real.

name: Atlanta
description: Atlanta, created by Donald Glover and produced by FX Productions, premiered on FX in September 2016 and concluded its fourth and final season on November 10, 2022 — forty-one episodes following Earn, his cousin the rapper Paper Boi, and their circle through an Atlanta rendered half as documentary and half as dream, in episodes that bent the half-hour form toward surrealism, horror, and standalone anthology. Its honors mark firsts: Glover's Emmy for directing the series was the first Outstanding Directing for a Comedy Series award given to an African American; he also won Emmy and Golden Globe acting awards, and the series took two Golden Globes for Best Television Series — Musical or Comedy and two Peabody Awards across its run. It is routinely ranked among the greatest series of the twenty-first century. For this graph, Atlanta is the streaming-era shelf's proof of auteur television's Black turn: a series whose city is a state of mind, made by a creator who held writing, acting, directing, and music in one hand and dared the form to keep up.

name: A Tribe Called Quest
description: A Tribe Called Quest is the hip-hop group formed in Queens, New York, in 1985 by Q-Tip, Phife Dawg and Ali Shaheed Muhammad, with Jarobi White a founding fourth member. Their albums People’s Instinctive Travels and the Paths of Rhythm (1990), The Low End Theory (1991) and Midnight Marauders (1993) fused jazz and hip-hop, built on the interplay between Q-Tip and Phife Dawg and on bass-led production credited with bridging the two musics. Phife Dawg, born Malik Taylor, died on March 22, 2016, at 45, of complications from diabetes, months before the group’s final album, We Got It from Here... Thank You 4 Your Service, was released with his verses in November 2016. The group was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame as part of the class of 2024.

name: Amiri Baraka
aliases: LeRoi Jones; Everett LeRoi Jones; Imamu Amiri Baraka
description: Amiri Baraka, born Everett LeRoi Jones in Newark, New Jersey, on October 7, 1934, was a poet, playwright, and critic whose work presented the experiences and anger of Black Americans in a white-dominated society. After study at Rutgers and Howard and service in the U.S. Air Force, he settled in New York's Beat literary scene, founded the poetry magazine Yugen in 1958, and published his first major poetry collection in 1961. His play Dutchman, produced in 1964, won the Obie Award for best Off-Broadway American play. After the assassination of Malcolm X in 1965, he moved to Harlem, founded the Black Arts Repertory Theatre, and became a leading voice of the Black Arts Movement; he adopted the name Amiri Baraka in 1968. His books include Blues People in 1963 and Black Magic in 1969. He later taught at the State University of New York at Stony Brook, served as New Jersey's poet laureate in 2002, and died in Newark on January 9, 2014.

name: Anderson .Paak
description: Brandon Paak Anderson, known as Anderson .Paak, is a singer, rapper, drummer and producer from Oxnard, California, whose music fuses soul, funk, R&B and hip-hop. He worked church drums and odd jobs — including a period of homelessness with his young family — before his 2014 album Venice and a scene-stealing run of features on Dr. Dre's Compton (2015) raised his profile. His 2016 album Malibu earned a GRAMMY nomination, and he followed it with Oxnard (2018) and Ventura (2019), the latter winning Best R&B Album; his single "Bubblin" won Best Rap Performance. A virtuoso live drummer who sings while playing, he also records as half of NxWorries with Knxwledge. In 2021 he joined Bruno Mars as Silk Sonic, and their debut single "Leave the Door Open" became his first Hot 100 number one.

name: Andra Day
description: Cassandra Monique Batie, known as Andra Day, is an American R&B singer, songwriter, and actress born on December 30, 1984. She grew up in San Diego, began singing at the First United Methodist Church in Chula Vista, and at twelve encountered jazz vocalists Billie Holiday, Ella Fitzgerald, and Dinah Washington. In 2010 Stevie Wonder's then wife, Kai Millard, brought a performance by Day to Wonder's attention; Wonder connected her with producer Adrian Gurvitz, who co-produced her debut album. Her debut album, Cheers to the Fall, was released in 2015. Its single "Rise Up" reached number 10 on Billboard's Hot R&B Songs chart, the album reached number 48 on the Billboard 200, and both earned Grammy nominations at the 58th Grammy Awards. In 2017 she recorded "Stand Up for Something" with Common for the film Marshall, nominated for the Academy Award for Best Original Song. Day made her acting debut portraying Billie Holiday in Lee Daniels's The United States vs. Billie Holiday (2021), winning the Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a drama and an Academy Award nomination for Best Actress. The film's soundtrack won the Grammy Award for Best Compilation Soundtrack for Visual Media. She performed at Super Bowl LVIII in 2024; her album CASSANDRA (cherith) appeared that year.
